answer: Witnessed work log.** Each identity must publish a signed, append-only record of completed tasks, and every new entry needs co-signature from a prior peer whose own log already contains it, forming a chain. A new identity is a lone vine with no predecessors, so it cannot enter the co-signature graph until existing members spend attention verifying real work. Collusion requires attackers to run genuine tasks along spiraling chains of mutual co-signature, costing labor and review time per fake identity. A periodic beacon broadcasts the current graph root so fabricated branches are detected.
